metadata.title: Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, Pemetrexed and Carboplatin Therapy
metadata.short_title: Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, Pemetrexed and Carboplatin Therapy
metadata.indication: First-line metastatic NSCLC in adults without a sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation. Current NCCP wording is histology-broad; the suitability of this pemetrexed backbone still requires explicit histology review.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

encoding_maturity.scope_note: Current official v4 PDFs audited including CTCAE v4 immune actions, 42-day schedule and component-specific chemotherapy rules. Partial assessment does not authorise treatment.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.histology_source_caveat: NCCP removed non-squamous from indication and eligibility in May 2025. The CheckMate 9LA whole-trial NSCLC result is not evidence that pemetrexed is suitable for every histology; confirm the actual backbone with the consultant.
metadata.schedule_summary: The first cycle lasts 42 days: all four medicines on Day 1, then nivolumab, pemetrexed and carboplatin on Day 22. Chemotherapy ends after those two visits. From Cycle 2, nivolumab continues on Days 1 and 22 and ipilimumab on Day 1 of each 42-day cycle. Immune treatment continues while appropriate until the cancer progresses, side effects require stopping, or up to 24 months without progression. Plans can change after review.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or other appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm all dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00713 Version 4. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: First-line metastatic non-squamous NSCLC without sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Cycle 1: nivolumab/pemetrexed/platinum Days 1 and 22 plus ipilimumab Day 1. Cycle 2 onwards: nivolumab Days 1 and 22 plus ipilimumab Day 1; up to 24 months without progression.

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

mucositis_grade.assessment_guidance: Inspect oral mucosa and assess pain, diet modification and ability to maintain oral intake.

pneumonitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated pneumonitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No pneumonitis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms; oxygen indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention such as ventilatory support required.

pneumonitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, oxygen requirement, imaging and exclude infection/alternative causes.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.label: Immune-mediated diarrhoea/colitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: Neither diarrhoea nor colitis is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Diarrhoea: fewer than 4 stools/day above baseline or mild ostomy-output increase. Colitis: asymptomatic, clinical/diagnostic observations only.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Diarrhoea: 4-6 stools/day above baseline or moderate ostomy-output increase; limits instrumental ADL. Colitis: abdominal pain or mucus/blood in stool.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Diarrhoea: at least 7 stools/day above baseline, incontinence, hospitalisation or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care ADL. Colitis: severe abdominal pain or peritoneal signs.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening diarrhoea or colitis; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_colitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess stool frequency over baseline, abdominal pain, blood/mucus, hydration, sepsis and peritoneal signs.

rash_grade.label: Immune-mediated rash/dermatitis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No rash. Use the most specific CTCAE skin term when a rash is present.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: For maculopapular rash: under 10% body-surface area, with or without symptoms such as itch, burning or tightness.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: For maculopapular rash: 10–30% body-surface area, or rash limiting instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: For maculopapular rash: over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, or limitation of self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 is not defined for uncomplicated maculopapular rash; use the appropriate severe cutaneous-reaction term if life-threatening features are present.

rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess morphology, body-surface area, symptoms, mucosal involvement and functional impact.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion-related reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess timing, intervention, airway or haemodynamic compromise and recovery.

eligibility: First-line metastatic NSCLC in adults without a sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation. Current NCCP wording is histology-broad; the suitability of this pemetrexed backbone still requires explicit histology review.
Histologically confirmed Stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with no prior systemic anticancer therapy; ECOG 0–1; adequate organ function.
Confirm histology suitability of pemetrexed and use current NCCP prior PD-1/PD-L1 guidance.
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the interactive assessment
monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal/liver profile, glucose, TFTs, HBsAg, HCV RNA and morning cortisol; hearing/CrCl if clinically indicated.
FBC and renal/liver profile before EACH Day 1 and Day 22 treatment; glucose and TFT before EACH 42-day cycle.
Ongoing symptoms and immune toxicity at each visit and between visits, including at least five months after last immune dose.
Disease monitoring follows the supervising consultant treatment plan; no invented fixed scan interval.
dose_modifications: All immune holds/stops apply jointly to nivolumab/ipilimumab. No immune dose reductions. Source Table 1 uses CTCAE v4.
Chemotherapy Table 3 uses current blood counts (nadir wording removed in v4). Dose changes are consultant decisions.
Pemetrexed dose levels 500 → 375 → 250 mg/m²; third reduction discontinue. Carboplatin AUC 6 → 5 → 4, or AUC 5 → 4 → 3; third reduction discontinue.
Pemetrexed below CrCl 45/dialysis and severe hepatic impairment are not recommended. Do not apply another regimen’s hepatic thresholds.

supportive_care.mapping_source: NCCP regimen v4 and NCIS antiemetics V8
supportive_care.mapping_basis: Induction high risk at both chemotherapy visits; immune-only Day 1 low (ipilimumab), Day 22 minimal (nivolumab alone).
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for moderate emetogenic risk
additional_supportive_care: Daily folate with lead-in and 21-day tail after last pemetrexed; B12 in preceding week; no automatic B12 maintenance after pemetrexed ends.
Immune alert card and at least five months post-treatment symptom vigilance.
